record.summary: Clear. A fresh post-pilot adversarial product, UI, and developer-experience challenge found no reproducible P0-P3 defect in the exact Dusk Developer Studio v1.0.19 release. When the final cross-platform chronology and targeted CV-D-026, CV-D-047, CV-D-069, and CV-D-038 receipts changed after the first challenge pass, the verdict was reopened for a real incremental review beginning after those gates; no finding reopened. The public npm bytes, repository identity, production manifest, assurance receipt, every deployed artifact, and recomputed production fingerprint agreed. The production UI preserved the Hosted-versus-local boundary, supported a truthful DuskDS Setup -> Access -> Build -> Inspect traversal without inventing build, wallet, deployment, or driver success, kept DuskEVM to one inert pre-launch surface, recovered honestly from a failed public-node request, and passed the independently exercised route, responsive, mobile WebKit, 200% zoom, keyboard, focus, forced-colors, reduced-motion, names, landmarks, headings, status, reset, disclosure, and Evidence-rail checks. The post-gate WebKit review independently reproduced the CV-D-038 invalidation: application navigation was CSP-clean and only Playwright screenshot instrumentation caused the blocked-style signal. The prior v1.0.18 challenge defects are closed in this candidate: the final browser bundle explicitly includes mobile-safari-webkit-emulation, and every DuskDS Evidence rail is a complementary landmark named by a visible Evidence heading.
